title: M13.9 — a remote frontier model route: sealed credential, daemon-proxied provider call, run-scoped model-mount token in the harness, non-possession on the execute receipt — BUILT; live acceptance blocked on the operator's provider credential
verdict: BUILT, bar OPEN: every clause of M13.9 the estate controls is green on the composed journey (route registered, custody crossing approved, key sealed, posture-only probe, env-key path refused, session bound at the daemon's /v1, run-scoped token issued and revoked, harness environment secret-free, plaintext absent from the state tree, provider call performed and receipted by the daemon); the PROVIDER refused the operator's credential, so no live run is recorded with its cost. Closure: a valid operator key and one run of the lane.

Fixed in the lane: the challenge is approved through the fixture approver (mintRecorded against the challenge's exact scope) and retried on the same idempotency key; the daemon-environment check narrowed to provider-key shapes.
runs 1-6 (recorded as they happened).run_2: 33/44: everything through the session binding green (execution_endpoint = the daemon's /v1), then the run failed CLOSED at 0 s with no_model_route — ExecutionSubstrate::probe() TCP-probed the daemon-wide env-default upstream (the local Ollama, not running) instead of the session's bound route. Fixed in the daemon: probe_for_session asks about the bound route (local: endpoint reachable; remote: sealed credential live) at the execute path and the session gate.
runs 1-6 (recorded as they happened).run_3: 42/44: the daemon proxied the call and receipted the provider's answer, but no usage came back. Two honesty findings surfaced by that and fixed before run 4: the App's run adapter marked a run 'done' on any HTTP 200 from execute even when the harness reported exit_status failure (now failed with the harness's typed error); the journey's 'writes at least one file' clause was satisfied by the environment's own .devcontainer scaffold (now excluded). The lane's detail was widened to show the provider's status.
runs 1-6 (recorded as they happened).run_4: 41/47: the receipt showed the provider's answer was 404 — the proxy posted to {base_url}/chat/completions while the registry normalizes base_url to the provider ROOT (a trailing /v1 is stripped at registration); the route-invoke transport addresses {base_url}/v1/chat/completions. Fixed in the proxy. The recovery clause also compared the run against an assumed 'done' instead of the pre-restart truth (fixed: it now reads the run's status before the kill).
runs 1-6 (recorded as they happened).run_5: 42/46: the provider answered 401 through the proxy — the operator's credential refused, the honest final state for the bar. A second finding: the run stayed 'running' for the whole 900 s poll and after the restart, although the daemon's execute lane had finished in seconds.
runs 1-6 (recorded as they happened).run_6: 42/46 with the work directory kept: the execute receipt shows the lane finished at 16:00:22.879 (exit_status failure, no_model_route, provider 401 receipted); the adapter's silent-authorization bump landed at 16:00:22.947 and the failure bump a millisecond later — two concurrent write-through fetches, and the daemon applied the OLDER record last, so the durable run record read 'running' with no failure entry, for every reader and across the serve restart. Fixed in the adapter: persistRun snapshots the record and chains writes per run, so the durable record can never regress behind an in-flight write.

mechanism.session_binding: an openai_compatible route binds a session only with a LIVE sealed credential (availability credentials_present on the sealed basis; `available` stays the local route's word); the binding's execution_endpoint is the daemon's own /v1 (IOI_HYPERVISOR_DAEMON_ADDR), never the provider URL
mechanism.proxy: POST /v1/chat/completions: a model id naming an active remote route with a live sealed credential is served by the daemon with that credential (bearer to {base_url}/chat/completions, stream forced off); the provider JSON is forwarded with route_id, receipt_id and transport; a model_invocation receipt carries transport, credential basis, providerStatus, providerModel and the provider's usage verbatim; non-2xx answers are refused 502 without echoing the provider body
mechanism.run_scoped_token: the session-execute lane mints a model-mount capability token for the run (audience = the session, grant = the lane receipt, allowed_scopes [model.chat:*], 2 h) through the kernel's own create operation, hands its NAME to the harness child as IOI_HYPERVISOR_MODEL_TOKEN, and revokes it when the lane returns; the harness shim presents it as the bearer
mechanism.non_possession: run_host_spawn_lane clears the child environment and sets exactly PATH, HOME, IOI_HYPERVISOR_MODEL_UPSTREAM and (remote only) IOI_HYPERVISOR_MODEL_TOKEN; the execute receipt lists those names (harness_environment_keys) and the transport (model_transport)
mechanism.preflight: the execute preflight asks about the SESSION's bound route (probe_for_session / session_bound_route_ready); an unbound session keeps the env-default probe
mechanism.process_environment_key_path: a route whose only credential is an env-key report is not executable (no sealed credential) and cannot bind a session (409 transport_unsupported_for_execution); the journey's daemon environment carries no provider key and no IOI_HYPERVISOR_ALLOW_ENV_PROVIDER_KEY opt-in
mechanism.composer: the /ai composer's CreateAgentSession accepts modelRouteRef and the adapter passes it to the daemon session create as model_route_ref (the New Session launcher already did)
mechanism.run_status: the App's run adapter reads the execute receipt's exit_status: a harness that reported failure is a failed run with its typed error, never 'done'; its write-through to the durable run record is ordered per run
